$comment: DISCLAIMER: This reference data is for informational purposes only. It records published approval and transition dates for cryptographic algorithms; it is not a security assessment. Dates sourced from a draft publication are marked sourceStatus: draft and may change.
description: Algorithm-lifecycle registry for archive timestamp chains (v3/common/archive-timestamp-chain.json). Every digest and signature algorithm id the chain schema accepts is listed here with a dated lifecycle: approved, then optionally deprecated, then disallowed. A step applies from its 'from' date inclusive. An RFC 4998 evidence record stays verifiable only while its newest archive timestamp uses algorithms that are not disallowed, so this registry is what a renewal check reads. scripts/check-archive-timestamp-chain.mjs keeps the schema's enums and this file in lockstep.

statuses.approved: Approved for generating new archive timestamps.
statuses.deprecated: Still allowed, but a renewal onto a stronger algorithm should be planned.
statuses.disallowed: Must not be used for a new archive timestamp. A chain whose newest link uses it needs renewal before it can be relied on.

profiles.cnsa-2.0: Listed in the NSA Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite 2.0 (September 2022): ML-DSA-87 for signatures, SHA-384 or SHA-512 for hashing. CNSA 2.0 expects exclusive use for web, cloud and operating-system categories by 2033 and full transition of national security systems by 2035.
